evidence: Prime Minister chairs the Central Traffic Safety Measures Council under Articles 14–15 of the Basic Act; the Cabinet Office coordinates its plan preparation and interministerial support.
qualification: Statutory executive chair, not attendance proof

evidence: The council roster names a minister for Financial Services, but NOT a separately named Finance Ministry seat. Public administration finances safety activities through ministry programmes; the 12th Plan does not set one audited, costed central council road-safety budget.
National Public Safety Commission chair is an express member; the National Police Agency prepares annual enforcement measures and accident-analysis priorities.
qualification: Formal public safety representation; operational enforcement by the NPA and prefectural police

evidence: Minister of Justice appears in the central council membership; the plan includes traffic-offence investigation, legal assistance and victim remedies.
qualification: Formal ministry seat; courts not directly members

evidence: Fire and Disaster Management Agency, local fire services, medical and rescue bodies are explicitly assigned rescue, first-aid and highway emergency response measures; the Fire Agency is not separately listed as a central council member.
qualification: Agency-level delivery through internal affairs and local governments

evidence: Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry is an appointed member and the plan expressly treats vehicle makers, advanced vehicle technologies, safety standards, inspections and recalls.
qualification: Formal industry portfolio, not manufacturers holding their own seat

evidence: MLIT road-construction and technical organizations are linked through road-works, design, inspection and safety measures; there is no separate construction trade/engineering association seat.
qualification: Technical engineering portfolio and implementing road authorities, not construction-membership seat

evidence: MLIT Minister formally holds a council seat; the plan places safety actions on national road authorities and prefectural road networks, including hazard removal, sidewalks and speed-management infrastructure.
qualification: Formal roads ministry portfolio with wider delivery network

evidence: MLIT Minister has a formal seat and the plan regulates professional drivers, commercial fleets and safe bus/truck services; operators are cooperating implementers, not statutory council members.

The Internal Affairs and Communications Minister is formally represented and the road plan describes ITS, road warnings and crash-data technologies, but no distinct Digital Minister is on the published member list.
qualification: Digital/communications technical link, not a dedicated digital-system member

evidence: No Environment Minister is included in the published council roster, and no independently accountable environmental road-safety function in the selected council mandate has been verified. The plan mentions emissions co-benefits of ITS but this is not an environmental-sector road safety coordination seat.
qualification: Environmental benefits are not formal membership

evidence: MLIT and local-government councils implement neighbourhood street redesign, universal design, pedestrian and cycling facilities; the central council does not list a separate urban planning or housing minister.
qualification: Urban/local planning interface rather than a distinct council seat

evidence: Health, Labour and Welfare Minister is a published member; health-sector emergency medical services, trauma care and rehabilitation are described in road plan pp. 92–102.
qualification: Formal ministerial portfolio; service delivery by medical/emergency actors

evidence: The Cabinet Office sought public comments, organized a hearing and separately solicited opinions from road-crash victims organizations for the 12th plan. Local traffic-safety associations and residents also participate in implementation.
qualification: Consultation and partnership documented, not standing nongovernmental central council membership

evidence: Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Minister formally holds a seat; the plan includes staged road-safety learning at nursery, primary, junior and senior secondary education levels.
qualification: Formal education ministry seat; schools implement curricula

evidence: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare portfolio and MLIT/NA​SVA-linked victim rehabilitation, counselling, care allowances and survivor assistance are explicit in the 12th plan; no dedicated social-protection council seat.
qualification: Named benefits and partner delivery, not separate formal social protection membership

evidence: Defense Minister is formally a member but that alone does not establish the ideal domain of civil defence, evacuation and mass-casualty coordination through the council. Road disaster planning appears as separate infrastructure work, not proof of this role.
qualification: Defence is not equivalent to road-safety civil-defence function
